a:r.a:t: Integral Membrane Proteins Have Selectively Placed Nonpolar Amino Acids Within the Membrane

p:cNvPr.descr: An image of transbilayer disposition of glycophorin in an erythrocyte. This image has a tube-like blue structure winding down, with various chemicals inside. Some have red hexagons above them, which will be identified as (hex) in this description. This tube changes to tan in the “outside” section, then back to blue on the inside portion of the image. It begins with amino terminus and has a 1 pointing to the beginning of the tube. Inside the tube, in order: Leu, Ser (hex), Thr (hex), Thr (hex), Glue, Val, Ala, Met, His, Thr (hex, Thr (hex), Thr (hex), Ser (hex), Ser (hex), Ser (hex), Val, Ser, Lys, Ser, Tyr, Ile, Ser (hex), Ser, Gin, Thr (hex), Asn (blue hex), Asp, Thr, His, Lys, Arg, Asp, Thr, Tyr, Ala, Ala, Thr (hex), Pro, Arg, Ala, His, Glu, Val, Ser (hex), Glu, Ile, Ser (hex), Val, Arg, Thr (hex), Val, Tyr, Pro, Pro, Glu, Glu, Glu, Thr, Glu, Glu. A 60 points to this Glu. It continues to Arg and Val. Next the tube-like structure winds down tighter than above and is in the “outside” and is tan. It begins with Gln and in order: Leu, Ala, His in blue circle, His in blue circle, Phe, Ser in blue cicle, Glu in blue circle, Pro, Glu in blue circle, Ile, Thr. There is a 74 pointing to this. It continues with Leu, Ile, Ile, Phe, Gly, Val, Met, Ala, Gly, Val, Ile, Gly, Thr, Ile, Leu, Leu, Ile, Ser, and Tyr. The tube continues in blue and is the “inside.” In order: Gly, Ile. There is a 95 pointing to this. It continues with Arg, Arg, Leu, Ile, Lys, Lys, Ser, Pro, Ser, Asp, Val, Lys, Pro, Leu, Pro, Ser, Pro, Asp, Thr, Asp, Val, Pro, Leu, Ser, Ser, Val, Glu, Ile, Glu, Asn, Pro, Glu, Thr, Ser, Asp, and Gln. This has a 131 pointing to it. The end of the tube is labeled as carboxyl terminus.
